subject: Philippine eagle
title: This Eagle Hunts Monkeys, and the Whole Species Lays About 250 Eggs a Year

scenes.text: The biggest eagle in the world eats monkeys. And it is losing a race it can't see.
The Philippine eagle. Three feet tall, a wingspan over two metres, claws three inches long. Locals called it the monkey-eating eagle.
It takes macaques, flying lemurs, civets, snakes, even monitor lizards, snatched from the treetops.
One pair needs up to 11,000 hectares of forest. That's forty square miles for one family.
And it lays one egg about every two years. The chick is fed for five months and stays close for over a year.
Fewer than 500 pairs are left. The forest shrinks faster than the eagle breeds. Each lost nest takes years to replace.

description:
The Philippine eagle is about a metre tall with a wingspan that can top two metres, and it hunts macaques, flying lemurs, civets, snakes and monitor lizards from the forest canopy.
A breeding pair needs roughly 4,000 to 11,000 hectares of forest and lays a single egg about every two years, feeding the chick for four to five months. Fewer than 500 breeding pairs are thought to remain, and killing one has been illegal since 1970.
Should a bird this rare be the national bird of a country? Comment below.
first_comment: A young Philippine eagle may not breed until it is five to seven years old, so every bird lost takes a decade to replace. Which giant bird should we cover next?
